rule: Negative results, falsified hypotheses and harness-invalid failures remain visible. Corrections add a superseding record or resolution; they do not delete the original outcome.

results.hypothesis: The retained Vite dependency-optimizer path can run under the strict guest CSP without JavaScript unsafe-eval.
results.finding: The dependency-optimizer court failed without JavaScript unsafe-eval and passed when unsafe-eval was admitted only to the isolated toolchain profile.
results.resolution: Keep the default strict profile and isolate unsafe-eval to the toolchain authority.

results.hypothesis: The initial P5 network policy unit helper correctly observes synchronous fail-closed authorization errors.
results.finding: The helper used assert.rejects as though authorize() failed asynchronously; the runtime correctly threw synchronously.
results.resolution: Wrap the action in Promise.resolve().then(action) without weakening synchronous fail-closed runtime semantics.

results.hypothesis: The initial hostile srcdoc preview fixture executes and reports its isolation result.
results.finding: The fixture emitted an escaped closing script token into actual HTML, so the HTML parser never closed the script and no postMessage occurred.
results.resolution: Emit a real closing script tag in the external harness source; keep sandbox isolation requirements unchanged.

results.hypothesis: Synthetic CDP Enter activation of the rendered P9 process-recovery control is stable under CI load.
results.finding: The rendered Chrome 153 court reached the failed-process recovery state, but synthetic CDP key activation did not complete process recovery before the 15 second harness deadline. PR #72 did not modify the product UI recovery handler, and the immediately preceding main CI #958 passed the same rendered recovery path.
results.resolution: Use deterministic DOM click activation on the actual production recovery button handler for the lifecycle-specific assertion. Keep keyboard, focus, IME and accessibility-tree coverage in the independent rendered interaction courts.
